findings.summary: USASpending: 20 federal contracts to Acronis entities totaling ~262K across FY2008-FY2016, zero spending after Acronis SCS formed
findings.detail: USASpending records show 20 federal contract awards to Acronis entities (Acronis Inc and Acronis International GmbH) totaling approximately 262,381 USD across FY2008-FY2016. Agencies included: DoD Army (67,940), DoD Navy (44,894), DoD Education Activity (35,972), VA (64,354), NIH (23,000), Treasury/IRS/OCC/Mint (8,919), DOT Maritime Admin (13,000), EPA (1,820). All contracts were small purchase orders for backup software licenses, maintenance, and True Image Server products. The USASpending timeline shows zero Acronis spending from FY2017 onward -- coinciding with Acronis SCS incorporation (Oct 2016) and SAM registration (March 2019). Acronis SCS has zero direct USASpending awards.

findings.summary: Acronis SCS had zero direct federal contract awards in USASpending despite being registered in SAM and holding DoDIN APL certification -- suggests sales through resellers/integrators or classified channels
findings.detail: Despite Acronis SCS being registered in SAM.gov since March 2019 (UEI Q87MPM4P1VM3) and holding DoDIN APL, Common Criteria, and FIPS 140-2 certifications, USASpending shows ZERO direct contract awards to Acronis SCS Inc. The pre-2017 contracts were all direct to Acronis Inc or Acronis International GmbH. After Acronis SCS was created as the government-facing entity, the public procurement record goes dark. This suggests one of several possibilities: (1) Sales went through reseller/integrator channels not directly attributed to Acronis SCS, (2) Contract vehicles were structured as subcontracts under larger primes, (3) Some procurement occurred through classified or intelligence community channels not publicly reported, or (4) The transition from direct parent sales to the SCS subsidiary structure changed the procurement approach. The DoDIN APL listing alone would have driven significant DoD purchases, but these do not appear in USASpending.

findings.summary: Acronis SCS achieved DoDIN APL, Common Criteria, and FIPS 140-2 certifications for Hardened Backup -- only full-disk backup solution on APL, deployed to air-gapped DoD systems
findings.detail: Acronis SCS Cyber Backup 12.5 Hardened Edition earned: DoDIN APL certification (April 2020), Common Criteria certification (August 2020), FIPS 140-2 validation (December 2020). It was the ONLY full-disk image backup and disaster recovery point solution on the DoDIN APL. Designed specifically for air-gapped no-internet environments: DoD weapons testing sites, development labs, training simulators, deployed tactical elements and warfighters, public utility SCADA systems. Also completed CMMC 2.0 Level 1 self-attestation. This means Acronis software -- from a company now excluded by DNI on classified grounds -- was the certified backup solution running on some of the most sensitive US military systems.

FASCSA order effective date July 11, 2025 but not published until September 15, 2025 -- two-month classified delay before public posting to SAM.gov
findings.detail: The DNI FASCSA exclusion order against Acronis AG went into effect on July 11, 2025, but was not published on SAM.gov until September 15, 2025 -- a gap of approximately 66 days. This delay suggests the order was initially classified or restricted, and agencies were notified through non-public channels before the public posting. The order itself provides no findings or rationale, which multiple law firms noted underscores the classified nature of the underlying intelligence. GSA removed Acronis from GSA Advantage on September 18, 2025 (three days after publication). Acronis SCS is not accepting new contracts. The order is indefinite.
